instructions: Boil about 3 1/2 cups of water in a kettle or small pot. Chop the onion and bell pepper fine. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and pepper and cook for 4 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Add the rice and stir for 3 minutes, until it smells toasty.
Add the chickpeas, the salt and the black pepper, then pour in 3 cups of the hot water. Turn the heat to high, stir once and bring to a boil.
Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed and small holes show on the surface. Don't stir.
Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version with a rating could be found, so Turkey's For Life's nohutlu pilav (no ratings yet) leads: onion and green pepper softened, rice toasted, canned chickpeas and hot water at 1 part rice to 2 parts liquid, then a covered rest. Almost Turkish Recipes (no rating) makes the tavuklu street version with butter and chicken broth. Water replaces chicken stock and the chicken is left out to keep it vegan.
